title: His first band at 15-16: house parties, advertising, brother on drums
summary: Trumpeters typically formed their own groups for house parties and advertising dances. Morand's band had his brother on drums and the bassist Chester Zardis.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, after you got out of school was when you started to play and earn it for professional purposes. Oh, yeah. Well, did you have your own band or did you play with someone else?

Well, I had my own band. Most of the trumpet players used to form their own band. You know, get a little group up together. Play house parties. Advertisements for dances and different things like that.
Advertisements for dances, was that like riding around in the wagon? Yeah, in a truck. Well, how old were you when you first got your own band?
Well, I guess I was around 16, 15. My brother, he's also a drummer. He learned how to play beat on steps and tin cans. He got large enough to buy them a set of drums.
Well, do you remember anyone else who was in your first band?
Yeah, Lowe Chester's artist, bass player. He's one of the great bass players of New Orleans. He's played with all the different bands. Buddy, Rene, Chris Kelly, and the different bands.
